title: Segmented prefix LRU+TTL hybrid orchestration with certifiable snapshotting
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem statement: As continuous batching amplifies reuse of short prefixes, our current global LRU creates noisy eviction behavior where high-throughput short-prefix cohorts thrash longer conversational prefixes. This translates to increased recompute, higher p99 micro-latency, and worse overall token cost for affected customers.

Goal: Define and prototype a segmented eviction orchestrator that blends per-prefix TTL heuristics with local LRU scoring per segment, plus a lightweight certifiable snapshot mechanism to verify correctness across asynchronous eviction/compaction passes. The orchestrator should preserve prefix linearizability guarantees for in-flight token KV reads and avoid unbounded memory growth on GPUs.

Scope: This ticket covers design, unit/integration test harness, a single-zone prototype on staging with GPU memory instrumentation, and a canary rollout plan for runtime-1.19. Not in scope: cross-region replication and dedicated cluster autoscaler integration (follow-up tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by infra and serving runtime reviewers
Prototype demonstrates <10% increase in p99 token latency due to eviction during stress compared to baseline and reduces recompute token rate by >=15% for short-prefix-heavy workloads
Automated invariant checker (snapshot verifier) passes for 1000 fuzzed eviction sequences without stale read violations
Unit tests cover segment boundaries, TTL expiry race windows, and prefix pin/unpin flows
Canary rollout plan with rollback criteria and dashboard defined
design_notes: We partition the global KV namespace into fixed 'segments' keyed by prefix hash ranges. Each segment maintains a local LRU ring and a TTL wheel. Segmentation reduces cross-prefix interference and lets eviction operate concurrently per segment.

Eviction policy: within a segment, perform a two-stage score: base_score = recency_score * recency_weight + access_frequency * freq_weight; final_score is shadowed by TTL_penalty if time_since_last_access > per-prefix_ttl_estimate. A background compaction pass drains low-score items in batches sized to GPU-friendly pages.

Certifiable snapshotting: before an eviction compaction, the segment emits a compact snapshot (compact manifest) containing item keys and epoch counters. The snapshot is signed locally and checkpointed to a small metadata store. Any in-flight request will check the manifest epoch to avoid reading an entry that the eviction has declared retired but not yet reclaimed.

Correctness guarantee: linearizability for KV GETs w.r.t. in-flight batching and eviction—reads either return value from before the compaction epoch or after rehydration; no intermediate stale state. The snapshot verifier asserts that no live references point to retired slots at reclaim time.

Memory model: reclamation occurs in two phases to avoid stalls: (1) logical retire (updates manifest + mark in allocator), (2) physical reclaim (actually free GPU slab) done asynchronously after ensuring no outstanding batch references. We use a lightweight reference epoch per batch to detect safety for reclaim.

Trade-offs considered: global LRU has simpler global optimality but higher lock contention and eviction thrash. Pure TTL is too coarse for bursty access. Segmented hybrid gives better locality at the cost of additional metadata and snapshot bookkeeping.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Prototype segment data-structures and per-segment background compaction loop; add TTL wheel and per-item meta (last_access, freq_estimate)
Week 2: Implement two-phase retire/reclaim flow and compact manifest emission; instrument GPU alloc/free metrics and record reclaim latencies
Week 3: Add snapshot verifier test harness and fuzzed eviction sequences; run stressbench against short-prefix-heavy workload generator
Week 4: Integrate with continuous batching path: ensure batch creation pins relevant prefixes and bumps segment epoch; add guard checks to avoid reclaiming pinned slots
Week 5: Address review feedback, harden unit tests, prepare canary rollout dashboard and playbook
test_plan: Unit tests: segment boundary conditions, TTL expiry races, pinned-prefix not reclaimed while pinned
Integration: staged stress test running mixed workloads (short prefixes, long convo prefixes, embeddings) for 4 hours capturing token recompute and p99 latency
Fuzzing: 1000 random eviction sequences with snapshot verifier enabled - assert no stale reads and no lost entries
Performance: measure GPU memory utilization, allocator churn, and reclaim latency under steady-state and burst scenarios
Canary: 2 host canary on staging with 1% production traffic mimic for 48 hours before wider rollout
rollout_plan: Step 0: Merge behind runtime feature flag 'segmented_eviction_v1'
Step 1: Internal staging canary: enable on staging clusters for 72h with synthetic workload and smoke tests
Step 2: Canary in production: enable on 0.5% of traffic for 48h, monitor regression metrics (p99 token latency, token recompute rate, OOMs)
Step 3: Gradual ramp to 10% over 24h if no regressions; then 50% over 48h, finally 100% after 7 days
Rollback criteria: >5% relative increase in p99 token latency or any production OOM in canary hosts or snapshot verifier failures
monitoring_and_alerts: Metrics to add: segment_evictions/sec, avg_reclaim_latency_ms, pinned_slots_count, snapshot_verifier_failures, token_recompute_rate
Dashboards: per-segment heatmap of memory pressure and eviction rate; global trend for token recompute and p99 latency
Alerts: alert when snapshot_verifier_failures > 0 (P0), or avg_reclaim_latency_ms > 200ms for 5m (P1), or OOMs detected on GPU host (P0)
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Nair: Kickoff - drafted initial design and rationale. Posted design doc to Confluence (see links). Requested reviewers from serving-runtime and allocator teams.

2026-03-11 Mariana Soto (reviewer): Questioned snapshot manifest storage cost and suggested embedding manifest into a compact ring on host memory to avoid extra RPC. Also suggested a TTL adaptation based on prefix percentiles rather than fixed heuristics.

2026-03-11 Liam Chen: Implemented segment structure and local LRU ring prototype. Early bench: reduced eviction-induced recompute for short-prefix generator by ~18% but increased avg eviction CPU by 6%.
2026-03-12 Alex Becker (allocator): Suggested using epoch-grant tokens tied to batching pipeline rather than per-request reference counting to reduce overhead. Will prototype epoch tokens in Week 2.

2026-03-12 Priya Nair: Added canary playbook draft and acceptance thresholds. Linked a Draft PR and Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/KV/Segmented+Eviction+Design and PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4827
